Karluk|United States of America.f: In 1890 Karluk had 1,123 residents, making it the third largest community in Alaska, just behind Juneau and Sitka.

Port Graham|United States of America.f: No road reaches Port Graham, so vehicles must come in by barge or ferry, and its Alutiiq name is Paluwik.

Nanwalek|United States of America.f: Aleksandrovsk, founded here in 1786 by Shelikhov's company, was the first Russian post on mainland Alaska.

Seldovia|United States of America.f: Its original Russian name Seldevoy means Herring Bay, and the land dropped six feet in the 1964 Good Friday earthquake.

Kwigillingok|United States of America.f: No roads lead to Kwigillingok, so its airport is the only connection to the outside world.

Tununak|United States of America.f: Tununak sits on Nelson Island in the Bering Sea, and a Roman Catholic mission was established there in 1891.

Akiachak|United States of America.f: Akiachak dissolved its city government in 1987 in favor of traditional village council governance.

Pilot Station|United States of America.f: Pilot Station sits on the lower Yukon River about eighty miles from the Bering Sea and was recorded in 1890 as Ankahchagmiut.
